_about: Legend: Urashima Taro (box from the sea), lines for H1+E1 (Jonny picked 26 Nov 23:11 Berlin). Speakers: N narrator, G grandmother, K kid, O Otohime, U Urashima, V old villager.

G.style: an old woman in her eighties, warm but stern, low slightly raspy voice, slow and calm

K.style: a twelve-year-old boy from a film, natural child actor, clearly a boy, voice not broken yet, curious and quietly worried, speaks clearly with crisp diction

O.style: a young noble woman, soft, kind and calm, a little sad, slow

U.style: a young man in his twenties, gentle fisherman, homesick, quiet

V.style: a very old village man, puzzled, dry and slow

lines: Never open a box from the sea.
In Japan, they tell of Urashima Taro, a young fisherman who saved a sea turtle from kids with sticks.
The turtle carried him down, to the Dragon Palace under the sea.
You saved my messenger. Stay as long as you like.
Every room had a window to another season. Spring. Summer. Autumn. Winter.
Every window is a year. He didn't count.
I have to see my mother.
Then take this. But never open it.
Then why give it to him?!
Back home, the pines were giants. Nobody knew his face.
Urashima? He drowned three hundred years ago.
His mother's grave was covered in moss.
But he was only gone three years...
Japan's ancient chronicle dates his voyage to the year 478. A shrine on that coast still keeps his box.
Scientists even named an effect after him. Fly near light speed, and you come home to a world that aged without you.
Alone on the beach, he hoped the box could take him back.
scared, pleading, clear voice, not whispering
White smoke. And three hundred years, in one breath.
It was never a gift. She had locked his years inside.
Grandma... did you ever open one?
